sections.label: Content note
sections.body: **Content note:** this page discusses the abuse of children and deaths in nursing homes. [Where to report abuse is listed below.](#kop-ri-report)

sections.label: Not the troubled teen industry
sections.heading: Not the troubled teen industry
sections.body:
Nursing homes are not part of the troubled teen industry, and Kids Over Profits does not track nursing homes or assisted living facilities.

This page is about where the two meet. They share a root: children were taken out of the almshouses they shared with old and disabled people, into institutions that became part of the industry. And some of the same private equity investors have owned both, and private equity's record in nursing homes shows what such owners do to a place that cares for people who cannot leave.

We are not experts on long-term care. Residents, their families, ombudsmen and the organizations listed below have done this work for decades.

sections.label: A shared root
sections.heading: A shared root
sections.body: For centuries elderly, sick and disabled people and poor children were held in the same workhouses and almshouses ([orphan care timeline](/orphanages/)). In the United States, Dorothea Dix investigated almshouses and jails from 1841 into the 1880s and found children, elderly people and people with mental illness confined together, and the children neglected, unschooled and exposed to physical and sexual abuse. Reformers moved the children out. New York's Children's Law of 1875 barred children aged 3 to 16 from county poorhouses, and disabled children went to institutions of their own, which became one of the roots of the troubled teen industry ([how the threads met](/birth-of-the-tti/)).

sections.label: The same owners
sections.heading: The same owners
sections.body:
The Carlyle Group and Onex have each owned a nursing home chain and a youth program company. Carlyle owned HCR ManorCare, one of the largest nursing home chains, from 2007[^1] until ManorCare went bankrupt in 2018 owing $7.1 billion,[^2][^3] and had invested in Newport Academy by 2017.[^4] It sold Newport to Onex, which bought a majority of Newport Healthcare in 2021 ([corporatization timeline](/corporatization/)).[^5]

Onex had owned both kinds of company before. In 2005 it bought Skilled Healthcare Group, then the operator of 70 nursing and assisted living homes in California, Texas, Nevada and Kansas;[^6] Skilled Healthcare merged into Genesis HealthCare in 2015.[^7] Onex took a stake in ResCare in 2004 and bought the rest in 2010.[^8] ResCare's filings describe residential treatment facilities, group homes and foster care for "young people with emotional and behavioral issues" and "juveniles in the justice system."[^9] ResCare was renamed BrightSpring Health in 2018;[^10] two West Virginia programs under the ResCare name are in our records.

What private equity does to nursing homes is known. A study of Medicare patients found that a private equity buyout raised a nursing home's patient mortality by about 11 percent; nurse staffing fell after the buyouts, which the authors name as one reason for the deaths.[^11] Private equity owners of care providers make each facility a separate legal entity, which limits the investors' liability, and load companies with debt to pay shareholders, which pushes facilities to cut staff ([corporatization timeline](/corporatization/)). The Senate Finance Committee found youth residential treatment run the same way, filling beds while cutting staff ([our summary](/warehouses-of-neglect/)).[^12]

If you know of another investor that has owned both nursing homes and youth programs, please [tell us](/contact/).

sections.label: Where to report abuse
sections.heading: Where to report abuse
sections.body:
- **If someone is in danger now**, call 911.
- **Long-Term Care Ombudsman.** Every state has one. Ombudsmen take complaints from nursing home and assisted living residents and their families, and work for the resident. Find yours through the Eldercare Locator, 1-800-677-1116, or [Consumer Voice's directory](https://theconsumervoice.org/get-help/).
- **State survey agency.** Complaints about abuse, neglect, too few staff or unsafe conditions in a nursing home go to the state survey agency, usually part of the state health department. CMS lists [each state's agency](https://www.cms.gov/medicare/health-safety-standards/quality-safety-oversight-general-information/contact-information), or call 1-800-MEDICARE, 1-800-633-4227 (TTY 1-877-486-2048), for the contact.
- **Adult Protective Services** takes reports of abuse, neglect and exploitation of older and disabled adults. Find your state's number through [NAPSA](https://www.napsa-now.org/help-in-your-area/).
- **Medicaid Fraud Control Units** investigate and prosecute [abuse and neglect of residents](https://oig.hhs.gov/fraud/medicaid-fraud-control-units-mfcu/) in facilities that take Medicaid.
- **Protection and Advocacy.** For disabled residents, including younger people who want to leave a nursing home, there is a [Protection and Advocacy agency](https://www.ndrn.org/about/ndrn-member-agencies/) in every state and territory.
- **988 Suicide and Crisis Lifeline**, 24 hours: call or text [988](tel:988).

For abuse in a youth program, see [our reporting directory](/report-abuse/).

sections.label: Organizations to learn from
sections.heading: Learn from the people who work on this
sections.body:
- [National Consumer Voice for Quality Long-Term Care](https://theconsumervoice.org/): Founded in 1975 as the National Citizens' Coalition for Nursing Home Reform; speaks for long-term care residents nationally and runs the National Long-Term Care Ombudsman Resource Center.
- [Long Term Care Community Coalition (nursinghome411)](https://nursinghome411.org/): Publishes nursing home staffing, inspection and antipsychotic data and guides for residents and families.
- [Center for Medicare Advocacy](https://medicareadvocacy.org/): A nonprofit law organization; tracks nursing home enforcement and residents' rights.
- [Justice in Aging](https://justiceinaging.org/): Legal advocacy for older adults with low incomes, including the rights of people living in nursing homes.
- [California Advocates for Nursing Home Reform](https://canhr.org/): Fact sheets, legal referrals and advocacy for people in California's long-term care facilities.
- [ADAPT](https://adapt.org/): A disability rights group, led by disabled people, that fights for the right to live at home instead of in nursing homes.

sections.label: Tell us if we got this wrong
sections.heading: Tell us if we got this wrong
sections.body: If you live or work in long-term care, or have a family member who does, and something here is wrong or missing, please [tell us](/contact/). We will correct it.

- ResCare, announcement of its purchase by Onex, filed with the SEC, 2010. [Filing](https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/776325/000095012310084472/y86520exv99w1.htm)
